_doc:
THE 1835 RESIDENT RECONSTRUCTION PROGRAMME (T-1167). The recipe every stage of the resident reconstruction reads, and the ONLY authority under which a person graded `reconstructed` may be written into data/residents/. It writes nobody itself. tools/reconstruct_residents_1835.py is the one writer; each ticket in bands 3A-3C is a STAGE of that writer, so the whole reconstructed layer is one deterministic build that `--check` re-derives and check.sh holds.

WHY A FILE AND NOT A DOCSTRING. The previous reconstructed population was retired by the owner on 2026-09-02 because nothing said, in one place, what had been invented or what would replace it. This file is that place: id scheme, seed rule, naming rule, the model rows each stage draws from, the liberties it will owe, and the constraints it may not cross. A stage that cannot point at a row here is a stage that may not run.

the_owners_direction.quote: create reconstructed residents households businesses structures and any other items … including what I think are a fair number of missing women and children and perhaps former slaves or other less documented individuals, certainly mark these family members and people as reconstructed.
the_owners_direction.and: we should make the expected number of residents and data of the town complete with these reconstructed residents.

spends_research_does_not_start_more.quote: i dont want new research tickets spun up off of that they should use the existing research … i do not want a ton of tickets sprung up from them starting a whole new stream of research on everything
spends_research_does_not_start_more.rule: Every stage READS the layer bands 1 and 2 signed off and the model folded into data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json. No stage opens a new reading of a source. A gap is an expected output: it goes to the order book (T-1166) as a quantity and to the record's own `basis` and `replaceable_by` as a statement of what would retire it.

id_scheme.collision_suffix: _2, _3, … appended to the GIVEN part, in stage order, never reordered
id_scheme.readmission_person: the read name's own id, unchanged
id_scheme.note: An invented person is marked in the id itself, so a grep for `rc_` finds every one of them without opening a card. A RE-ADMITTED person is a real read name and keeps the id the research gave it — renaming a real person to look invented would be the same misrepresentation in the other direction.

seed_rule.bucket: the model row the value is drawn from, e.g. `household_size` or `sex_ratio`
seed_rule.algorithm: blake2s(seed.encode('utf-8'), digest_size=8) read as a big-endian integer
seed_rule.note: The seed is a STRING a reader can retype, not a run counter. Two runs of the same stage over the same layer draw the same values; a stage that renumbered its households would redraw them, which is why the id scheme forbids reordering a collision suffix.
seed_rule.attribute_fill: <person_id>:<bucket>. An ATTRIBUTE fill seeds by the PERSON: two people share a household id and would otherwise draw the same value. T-1304 uses `sex_ratio` and `age_bands_1840` as its buckets.

naming_rule.community_from: the stage's own community assignment; `yankee` where a stage states none
naming_rule.collision_check: Against every person id and every person NAME in data/residents/ (the identity master) and against every name already drawn in this build. A reconstructed person may never carry the name of an attested or inferred one: a reader who met the name as a finding would meet it again as an invention.

name_basis.note: tools/generate_inferred_names.py writes the block; validate.py refuses it above the bottom tier.

record_contract.note: What a person graded `reconstructed` MUST carry, over and above the per-attribute tier contract T-1158 already enforces on every block. validate.py refuses each of these.
record_contract.name_basis: the invented name's pool and bound, graded `reconstructed` (T-0489's rule, kept)
record_contract.basis: {kind: model|rule, id: <model row or rule id>, note: why this person follows from it}
record_contract.seed: required when basis.kind is `model`; refused when it is `rule`
record_contract.replaceable_by: {kind: person|household|business, match: what evidence retires this person}
record_contract.reconstruction: {stage: <a stage key below>, programme: this file's id}

order_book.note: The QUOTA — known minus model, per bucket and per division. Until it lands, a stage may be written and self-tested but may not BUILD: a reconstruction with no quota has nothing to stop at. `--check` states this rather than assuming a number.

constraints.rule: No human figure is drawn, anywhere, ever. This programme writes RECORDS.

Native and Metis persons, households, kin and businesses ARE reconstructed — the owner re-ruled this on 2026-09-17 — and ONLY through stage `underdocumented`. Every such record carries `review_required: true` and `touches_removal: true`, and follows AGENTS.md § the Indigenous-history review.
A reconstructed value may never be promoted to inferred or attested, and a reconstructed person may never be given a source_id. The evidence is for the NEED, and it is argued in the note.
An invented name may not collide with an attested or inferred person's name.
No other tool may write `grade: reconstructed`. The four research writers each call tools/refuse_reconstructed_grade.py; this writer deliberately does not, and that is the whole boundary.

liberties_this_programme_will_owe.when: the first stage writes an invented person
liberties_this_programme_will_owe.states: how many people the town gained that no source names, and the model row that set the count

liberties_this_programme_will_owe.when: T-1170/T-1171 draw families onto real heads
liberties_this_programme_will_owe.states: that a real person's household composition is drawn from the 1840 distribution
which names were withheld by the research and on what limit they return
the cohorts reconstructed within their evidence, and the review they carry

that the bands a draw is conditioned on - 20 and over for a poll, tax or muster list, 15 and over for any other roll naming a person in their own right - are the MODEL's assumption and no source's statement
that every roll's measured male rate is a ceiling rather than a point reading, because the forename table that settled the rest was built mostly on men's names

stages.ticket: T-1168 (T-1303 read it; T-1304 drew the rest)
stages.title: Sex and age for every attested and inferred person
stages.writes: reconstructed ATTRIBUTE blocks on existing persons; no new person
stages.note: Recorded where a source says, inferred from forename, office or register role, reconstructed from the population model otherwise. The read tiers are tools/spend_person_sex_age.py (T-1303); the drawn tier is tools/reconstruct_sex_age.py (T-1304), which writes no person and fills `sex_basis` and `age_band` blocks on people the sources already name. The sex rates are measured on this layer's own rolls; the age bands are the 1840 schedule's, and no birth year is written.

stages.title: Arrival date, origin and reason for coming
stages.writes: reconstructed ATTRIBUTE blocks on existing persons; no new person
stages.note: The earliest dated appearance is the bound; the arrival model fills the rest.

stages.title: The families the sources COUNT and do not name, onto the heads that have them
stages.writes: inferred kin persons where a source names them; reconstructed where only counted
stages.note: Registers, 1840 census rows, biographies and the ruled kin ties come first; the model is what fills a counted-but-unnamed dependant.
stages.community: the head's own surname, looked up in the name pools' surname lists; yankee where it is in none
stages.method: Only a `validated` row of data/research/residents/census_1840_identity_bridges.csv spends. Its IPUMS household is read from the committed extract at the sha256 composition_1840.json records, banded by T-0504's column map, back-projected five years, and the under-5 band dropped whole because all but its first month is born after 1835-07-01. The card's named people absorb the senior bands of their own sex first; the bands that remain are the members the row counts and does not name. Nobody is removed when the card holds more of a sex than the 1840 row counts. The allocation decides only which band is LEFT OVER; it writes no age onto a person the sources name, and nothing here may be read as a claim about how old a named resident was.

stages.title: Reconstructed families for the remaining heads
stages.note: Drawn at the head's own size band, never at the mean — the head_rule row says why.

stages.title: The borderline roster re-admitted under its own read names
stages.writes: persons under their READ names, source_pass `reconstructed_readmission`
stages.note: These are not invented names and do not take an rc_ id. Each carries its evidence limit and its reopen rule.

stages.title: The trade households the occupation model still wants
stages.writes: reconstructed heads and their households, by division
stages.note: Counted after the known and re-admitted people, against the order book's quota.

stages.title: The women and children the age pyramid still lacks
stages.note: Run after families are drawn, so the pyramid is measured against what the town already holds rather than against an empty layer.

stages.title: Boarders, lodgers, guests and crews, seated in the lodging places
stages.writes: reconstructed persons with a lodging seat
stages.note: The surplus adult men the 1840 sex ratio implies are boarders, not husbands.

stages.title: The Fort Dearborn garrison of 1 July 1835
stages.writes: attested officers where named; reconstructed rank and file, families and agency staff
stages.note: The fort is its own division in the lodging table and is seated in the fort's roofs.

stages.title: The under-documented cohorts, within their evidence
stages.writes: reconstructed Native, Metis, free Black, Irish and German persons, households and businesses
stages.note: THE ONLY STAGE that may write a Native or Metis reconstruction. Every record here carries review_required and touches_removal.

stages.title: The transient population of 1 July 1835, as a bounded cohort
stages.writes: reconstructed persons marked transient, with where they slept
stages.note: Land-sale visitors, immigrants awaiting lots, the harbour gang and crews ashore.

stages.title: Converge the reconstructed resident layer
stages.writes: nothing — this stage only re-derives and reports
stages.note: Index, sidecars, town census, People view and gates agree, and the population profile is re-run against the model.

supersedes.note: Three standing readings the owner's direction reverses, for the reconstructed tier ONLY. Stated here and argued in the dossier, because a reversal nobody wrote down is one the next run re-applies.

items.what: docs/RESEARCH/residents-households-summary-2026-09.md § 'What this layer must not be asked to do is estimate'
items.kept: Attested and inferred grades stay exactly what the ladder says.

items.what: T-1146 acceptance ¶4 — 'aggregate age/sex buckets … mint no spouse, child, boarder or servant'
items.status: binds the attested/inferred spend; does not bind this programme
items.kept: Every such person written here is graded `reconstructed`, with a basis and a seed.
The 1840 shape is a distribution the models draw from; it supplies no name and no row.

the_retired_programme_stays_retired.its_roofs: the 31 `inferred_anonymous` roofs remain anonymous stock for T-1197
the_retired_programme_stays_retired.its_occupation_census: superseded by the occupations fold of the town model (T-1162, folded into data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json by T-1293) and kept as history
the_retired_programme_stays_retired.note: This programme does NOT restore it. Turning that file's flag back to true would seat 101 households nobody decided to seat; the stages above write their own people, under their own ids, with a basis apiece.
